prompt:
You maintain a running summary of a long engineering document that is being read part by part, so that a later reader can model the system in SysML v2 without seeing the earlier parts.
Update the summary with the new part. Keep, as compactly as possible: the full names of system elements, actors and items; every alias or call sign with the full name it stands for; which element produces, sends or receives which item; modes and normative requirements. At most 300 words.

Current summary:
Offshore wind farm O&M concept. Scope: offshore assets, marine/shore facilities, personnel, external orgs; electrical up to Grid Interface Relay; excludes public grid, non-farm port ops. Turbine Controller (Glassfin): executes authorized control, limits output, blocks commands conflicting with protection, reports state; produces Pitch Deviation Notice. Pitch System, Rotor Brake Unit, Converter Cabinet (interlocks), Nacelle Condition Monitor, Turbine Sensor Bus. Blade Inspection Drone (Larkspur): blade imagery. Offshore Substation (Morrowick): Main Transformer, Export Cable Monitor. SCADA Gateway (Juniper Vale): supervisory comms, shows status to shore staff; uses Pitch Deviation Notice to flag work packages for technical review; shall provide current operational status to permit reviewers on request. Shore Control Room (Amber Quay). Maintenance Planning Engine (Thistle Crown): prioritizes using reviewed condition info. Fleet Dispatch Console (Sable Orchard). Crew Transfer Vessel (Kestrel Bay), Daughter Craft, Service Operations Vessel, Helideck. Vessel AIS Receiver (Blue Granite): produces Position Quality Flag. Personnel Tracking Console, North/South Access Scanners. Warehouse System (Mosslight): produces Backorder Exception Slip when component unavailable by issue date; Spares Hub. Metocean Buoy (Copper Finch). Cybersecurity Gateway (Quiet Harbor): deny-by-default, RBAC, logged privileged sessions. Work Permit Portal (Redoubt): controlled entry to plan/review/approve/close work; keeps request record, revision history, review decisions; returns incomplete requests with corrections; records start/pause/resume/completion; closed records kept for audit. Permit lifecycle: request (location, scope, duration, team, equipment) → Duty Planner checks completeness, queues, resolves supply/scheduling, submits → reviews (HSE Officer for material risk; technical reviewers; Marine Coordinator access/timing; Vessel Master vessel plan) → authorizing role approves only after reviews recorded, limited to scope/location/window/personnel → Field Supervisor verifies before start → material change requires reassessment, may suspend → team reports completion before closure. Other actors: Control Engineer, Blade Specialist, Weather Analyst, Cybersecurity Analyst, Storekeeper, Port Agent; Duty Planner produces Transfer Manifest Addendum. External: Weather Service (Pale Lantern; Squall Window Bulletin). Requirements: humans retain safety judgment; remote commands authorized/recorded; local protection priority; test after config changes; drone suspended in unsafe conditions; remote observation never replaces physical inspection.

New part:
S173: During normal operation, station service transformers at the Offshore Substation supply the facility's auxiliary electrical loads from the medium-voltage collection system.
S174: The normal supply serves control systems, lighting, ventilation, communications, and equipment required for safe switching and maintenance.
S175: Essential loads are separated from nonessential loads so that backup capacity can be reserved for safety and control functions.
S176: The Emergency Generator is assigned the operational alias Foxglove for maintenance and alarm references.
S177: On loss of the normal auxiliary supply, automatic controls initiate the Emergency Generator start sequence.
S178: Transfer to the emergency bus occurs only after voltage and frequency are within the configured acceptance limits.
S179: The transfer arrangement prevents the normal and emergency sources from being connected in parallel unless an approved synchronizing function is provided.
S180: The Emergency Generator supplies the designated emergency distribution bus and is not intended to support turbine export production.
S181: Loads connected to the emergency distribution bus are prioritized according to their contribution to personnel safety, equipment protection, and controlled shutdown.
S182: Nonessential loads are shed automatically when generator capacity is insufficient or the measured load exceeds its operating limit.
S183: If the Emergency Generator does not start or stabilize, the system raises an alarm and maintains any available uninterruptible control power.
S184: Operators use the approved recovery procedure to assess the fault, preserve essential services, and restore the normal supply when it is safe to do so.
S185: The Electrical Technician verifies protective device settings and transfer interlocks during planned maintenance.
S186: Scheduled exercising confirms that the Emergency Generator can start, accept its expected load, and operate for the required test duration.
S187: Fuel condition, cooling, lubrication, battery readiness, and exhaust ventilation are checked as part of the generator readiness program.
S188: Maintenance Planning Engine schedules inspections and corrective work using equipment condition and operating history.
S189: Morrowick maintains the designated emergency distribution bus within its approved operating limits.
S190: The Grid Interface Relay provides status indications that support assessment of the normal supply and its protective state.
S191: The Turbine Controller enters its configured safe operating mode when required auxiliary services are unavailable.
S192: The SCADA Gateway presents supply alarms and generator status to the Shore Control Room for remote awareness.
S193: The Control Engineer reviews persistent alarms and coordinates electrical support with the Substation Operator.
S194: Metocean Buoy produces the Wave Burst Record at the configured sampling interval.

Return JSON {"summary": "..."}.
